newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KHABIBULIN RECORDS SEVENTH SHUTOUT AS COYOTES BLANK LEAFS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-KHABIBULIN RECORDS SEVENTH SHUTOUT AS COYOTES BLANK LEAFS.

text.p: Nikolai Khabibulin stopped 33 shots to record his league-leading seventh shutout of the season and Jeremy Roenick scored twice as the surging Phoenix Coyotes blanked the Toronto Maple Leafs 3-0 on Saturday.
Khabibulin was at his sharpest in the third period when he turned back 14 shots, including a semi-breakaway by Mats Sundin.
The win was the fourth in five games for Phoenix, which moved above the .500 mark at 35-34-5 and into fourth place in the battle for Western Conference playoff positions.
Jocelyn Lemieux's first goal of the season gave Khabibulin all the offence he needed, but Roenick added his 24th goal in the second period and 25th in the third.
"The most important thing is that we win," said Khabibulin, who was less concerned with his shutout tally.
Toronto goalie Felix Potvin made 41 saves in a losing effort.
In Pittsburgh, Bobby Holik's goal with 8:02 remaining in the third period lifted the New Jersey Devils to a 3-2 victory over the Penguins.

Holik fired a rebound from the left circle over the glove of goaltender Patrick Lalime to snap a 2-2 deadlock as the Devils moved into a tie for first-place in the Eastern Conference with Philadelphia on 91 points.
Dave Andreychuk's 25th goal midway through the second period pulled New Jersey within 2-1 and the Devils dominated the final period, outshooting the Penguins 18-5.
Dave Ellett scored the tying goal at 3:43 of the third.
On Long Island, Todd Bertuzzi and Claude Lapointe scored 24 seconds apart in the third period as the New York Islanders rallied for a 3-3 tie with the Philadelphia Flyers.
Philadelphia squandered a 3-0 lead and a chance to retain sole possession of first place in the Eastern Conference.

The Flyers played most of the game without star centre Eric Lindros, who suffered a left leg injury early in the game after being checked by Islanders defenceman Rich Pilon, who received a major penalty and was ejected.
Paul Coffey, John LeClair, who notched his 47th goal, and Daniel Lacroix staked the Flyers to a 3-0 first-period lead.

In Boston, Steve Duchesne scored a pair of powerplay goals and the Ottawa Senators built a three-goal lead and held on for a 5-4 victory over the Bruins to edge closer to a playoff spot in the Eastern Conference.

The Senators snapped a 2-2 tie on goals by Shawn McEachern, Tom Chorske, and Alexei Yashin and moved within three points of Washington and Montreal in the hunt for the final playoff berth in the East.
Jozef Stumpel scord twice for the Bruins, who are likely to miss the playoffs for the first time in 30 years.

At Florida, Ray Sheppard scored the go-ahead goal midway through the second period and set up Radek Dvorak's game winner just over five minutes later as the Panthers held on for a 3-2 victory over the Buffalo Sabres.

John Vanbiesbrouck had to make only 16 saves for the Panthers, who killed off six Buffalo power plays and limited the Sabres to just one shot during a four-minute man advantage early in the third period.
Scott Mellanby scored the other Florida goal. Miroslav Satan had a goal and an assist for Buffalo.
In Montreal, Rick Tocchet netted a pair of goals and Bill Ranford stopped 28 shots as the Washington Capitals beat the Canadiens 3-1 to tighten the bottom of the Eastern Conference playoff race.
Steve Konowalchuk added a short-handed tally for the Capitals, who are 3-0 against Montreal this season.
The win moved Washington into a tie with the Canadiens for the final two playoffs spots in the East with 66 points.
Martin Rucinsky scored the lone goal for Montreal.
In Los Angeles, Vitali Yachmenev and Nathan Lafayette spearheaded an outstanding special teams effort by the Kings and Byron Dafoe turned aside 34 shots in a 2-1 victory over the San Jose Sharks.

Yachmenev scored a powerplay goal with 11 seconds left in the first period and Lafayette added a short-handed tally midway through the second for the Kings, who successfully killed off all six San Jose power plays.
Jeff Friesen scored his 26th goal for San Jose, which has lost six of its last seven contests.
In Vancouver, Adrian Aucoin and Markus Naslund scored second-period goals and Corey Hirsch made 30 saves to lead the Canucks to a 3-2 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Martin Gelinas had the other goal and Lonny Bohonos picked up a pair of assists for the Canucks, who are 8-1 all-time against Tampa Bay.
Chris Gratton and John Cullen scored for the Lightning.
